summary.goal: Add an 'Active Channels' section to the left sidebar that shows relay channels with recent activity (~5 minutes), and a full channel view page at /channels/#<id> copied from relay-dashboard.
summary.context:
The planner-ui needs visibility into agent relay activity. Currently users can't see which channels have active conversations. The relay-dashboard already has a mature channel view implementation (ChannelViewV1, ChannelChat, etc.) that can be adapted for planner-ui.

Existing backend infrastructure:
- GET /api/channels - Lists channels the user is a member of (src/api/handlers/channels.ts)
- GET /api/channels/:id/messages - Fetches message history for a channel
- GET /api/channels/:id/presence - Returns online members
- WebSocket proxy at /ws - Proxies to relay daemon for real-time updates (src/relay/ws-proxy.ts)
- Channel management module (src/relay/channels.ts) - Creates #planner and #plan-{id} channels

Key constraint: Agent-relay filters channels by membership. Users only see channels they've joined. Plan channels are created when plans are created, but users need to be auto-joined when they view a plan.
problem_evidence: No visibility into active relay channels from the planner UI
Users must use relay-dashboard separately to monitor agent conversations
No way to quickly navigate to active channels where agents are working

acceptance_criteria.description: 'Active Channels' section appears in sidebar below Navigation section
Shows channels that have had activity in the last ~5 minutes
Each channel shows: channel name (#name format), unread count badge if any
Clicking a channel navigates to /channels/#<id>
Active channels section collapses when sidebar is collapsed (icon-only mode)
/channels/:channelId route renders the channel view
Channel view shows: header with channel name, message list, message input
Messages display sender avatar, name, timestamp, content in Slack-style layout
Can send messages via the input (uses relay sendChannelMessage)
Real-time updates: new messages appear without refresh
Empty state when no active channels
Avatar shows color-coded initial (purple for users, cyan for agents)
Messages from same sender within 5 min are grouped (avatar only on first)
Date dividers appear between message groups ('Today', 'Yesterday', date)

summary.approach_rationale: The relay-dashboard channel implementation is mature and handles many edge cases. Copying and adapting is faster than rebuilding, and ensures UX consistency. The out-of-scope features can be removed or gated.

design_decisions.decision: Copy relay-dashboard components rather than build from scratch
design_decisions.rationale: Faster implementation, proven code, handles edge cases. User explicitly requested this approach.

design_decisions.decision: Use existing useRelay context instead of creating separate WebSocket
design_decisions.rationale: Planner-ui already has RelayProvider with shared connection. Reuse it rather than duplicate.
alternatives_considered: Copy useChannels hook with its own WebSocket

design_decisions.rationale: Balance between showing recent activity and not showing stale channels. Can be adjusted based on UX feedback.

design_decisions.decision: Auto-join users to plan channels when viewing plans
design_decisions.rationale: Agent-relay only shows channels where the user is a member. Without auto-join, users won't see plan-specific channels even if they have access to the plan. The channel membership is persisted via _channelMembership metadata in relay's JSONL storage.
alternatives_considered: Show all channels regardless of membership

design_decisions.decision: Use existing channel REST endpoints (GET /api/channels, GET /api/channels/:id/messages)
design_decisions.rationale: These endpoints already exist in src/api/handlers/channels.ts and provide initial channel list and message history. No need to duplicate this logic in the frontend or create new endpoints.
alternatives_considered: Query relay storage directly from frontend

design_decisions.decision: Use existing WebSocket proxy at /ws for real-time updates
design_decisions.rationale: The backend already proxies WebSocket connections to the relay daemon via src/relay/ws-proxy.ts. Real-time message subscriptions should use this existing infrastructure.

design_decisions.decision: Adopt relay-dashboard's Slack-style message layout with avatars and grouping
design_decisions.rationale: Initial implementation was too minimal (simple chat bubbles). The relay-dashboard styling with avatars, message grouping, and date dividers provides better UX consistency and visual richness. Copy the proven patterns rather than reinvent.
design_decisions.change_reason: User feedback: channel view looks too plain compared to relay-dashboard
